coverImage.alt: Her Waka June 2026 — Personal Branding & Growth Tips, delivered by SheSharp, Ministry of Social Development and academyEX

events.shortDescription: The fourth HER WAKA cohort focuses on personal branding and career growth strategy with Andrea Halal — learn to treat your career like a Go-To-Market plan and use LinkedIn to build visibility, credibility, and genuine professional networks.

detailPageData.title: Her Waka (June 2026) — Personal Branding & Growth Tips
detailPageData.subtitle: Personal Branding & Growth Tips
fullDescription: The fourth cohort of the HER WAKA series focuses on personal branding and career growth — treating your career like a Go-To-Market strategy.

Andrea Halal, Tech Marketing Leader at Ideqa and creator of Big Leap Energy, will share how she rebuilt her network and professional credibility after moving to New Zealand with no local connections. Drawing on nine years of marketing experience across TV, production, advertising, brand management, and B2B marketing, Andrea will walk participants through the practical steps for building visibility and trust when you are new, relocating, or pivoting.

Expect a grounded, strategy-driven session on using LinkedIn as a career tool (not a highlight reel), on why positioning matters as much as performance, and on how relationships quietly compound over time.
As with every HER WAKA cohort, RCSA will join the session to share insights on the current New Zealand job market and offer practical guidance on job-seeking.

HER WAKA is a dynamic, employment-focused programme delivered by SheSharp in Auckland for Ministry of Social Development clients who are ready to strengthen their pathway into work. Running monthly from March to June 2026, each session is a cohesive, repeatable event designed to build job readiness, confidence, and practical understanding of the New Zealand labour market.

speakers.name: Andrea Halal
speakers.title: Tech Marketing Leader | Building Your Career GTM Strategy
speakers.bio: Andrea Halal is a Tech Marketing Leader at Ideqa driving B2B growth across ANZ, and the creator of Big Leap Energy — a career Go-To-Market methodology for tech professionals building visibility, credibility, and networks from scratch. After relocating to New Zealand with no local connections, she applied marketing thinking to her own career and rebuilt from zero. She is Ambassador Lead and Operations Strategy at The Marketing Club AU/NZ, writes and speaks on personal branding, LinkedIn as a career tool, and the mindset of showing up before you feel ready.

specialSections.title: What to Expect
content: Inspirational speakers sharing authentic employment journeys and practical lessons from navigating the New Zealand workforce
Employer and recruiter panels offering direct insight into current hiring expectations
Practical job-readiness sessions focused on professional presentation, interview confidence, and effective employer engagement
Clear and accessible employment rights guidance
Structured networking opportunities with employers, recruiters, and industry representatives

events.title: Making Linkedin Work for You

coverImage.alt: Making LinkedIn Work for You with Stuart Little event cover

events.shortDescription: A masterclass to help you build a strong personal brand on LinkedIn and attract the right opportunities.

detailPageData.title: Making LinkedIn Work for You with Stuart Little, presented by She Sharp and AUT
detailPageData.subtitle: Presented by She Sharp and AUT (Engineering, Computer and Mathematical Sciences)
fullDescription: In today’s changing world of work, your LinkedIn® profile is more than a CV. It is your personal brand, your digital presence and often the first impression you make before a conversation even begins.
Opportunities are no longer only applied for — they are discovered. Recruiters, hiring managers and businesses are actively searching for people with the right skills, mindset and visibility.
How you show up on LinkedIn directly influences what finds you.

This session is led by Stuart Little, Creative Strategist and Director of Agency8. Through his work supporting professionals, businesses and large-scale programmes across New Zealand, Stuart brings a real-world perspective on how LinkedIn is actually being used today to identify, assess and connect with talent for a changed job market.

Rather than focusing on theory, this workshop draws on practical insight, current hiring trends and proven strategies that help people move from having a profile to building a presence that creates momentum.
You will gain a clearer understanding of how to position yourself, how to be found, and how to use LinkedIn as a tool that works for you consistently.

This session will provide the knowledge to build a LinkedIn® presence that reflects who you are, what you do, and how you work. The focus is not just on creating a profile, but on positioning yourself in a way that attracts the right opportunities and builds long-term career momentum.
This workshop is presented in partnership with She Sharp and AUT (Engineering, Computer and Mathematical Sciences) as part of New Zealand’s Digital Suite.

speakers.name: Stuart Little
speakers.title: Creative Strategist and Director of Agency8
speakers.bio: Stuart Little, Creative Lead for the THRIVE and Director of Agency8. Through his work supporting professionals, businesses and large-scale programmes across New Zealand, Stuart brings a real-world perspective on how LinkedIn is actually being used today to identify, assess and connect with talent for a changed market.

speakers.name: Janelle Wright
speakers.title: Founder of Janelle's Recruitment
speakers.bio: Janelle Wright is the founder of Janelle's Recruitment. She helps professionals stand out and land the right roles through personal branding, ATS-optimised CVs, LinkedIn strategy, interview coaching and proactive recruitment. Her process works. 90% of candidates secure roles, she's built a strong industry network and her LinkedIn following has grown past 9,000. Janelle has worked and coached for major global brands around the world. She takes a people-first approach with real pace behind it, so candidates don't just find a job they build a career.

specialSections.title: What You’ll Learn
content: How to build a strong personal brand on LinkedIn®
How to position your skills and experience with clarity and relevance
What employers and recruiters are actually looking for in 2026
How to create a profile that attracts the right opportunities
How to move from simply having a profile to building a visible, active presence

specialSections.title: Why Attend
content: Gain practical insights to improve your LinkedIn® presence, build confidence in how you show up online, and learn how to attract — not chase — opportunities.

events.title: From Burnout to Balance

coverImage.alt: From Burnout to Balance event cover

events.shortDescription: An event exploring strategies for managing burnout and finding balance in your career and life.

detailPageData.title: From Burnout to Balance
fullDescription: Our “From Burnout to Balance” breakfast event is going to be an enlightening morning where we delve into two vital aspects of well-being. As women, we wear many hats - we are professionals, mothers, partners, and more. It is this dance of roles that showcases our adaptability, but also puts us at a greater risk of burnout. In addition, the boundaries between work and personal life are becoming increasingly blurred.

Our incredible speakers will guide you on a journey towards achieving equilibrium in the fast-paced world of technology, looking at actionable strategies to harmonise professional ambitions with self-care.

Brigette McGregor-Macdonald will speak to discovering the power of mindfulness and provide key techniques that empower you to stay centred, enhance focus, and build resilience against burnout.‍ Maya Lee will dive into the critical connection between nutrition, health and stress management, providing insights into putting your health first for peak performance, optimising energy levels and warding off burnout. It is time to invest in your well-being, embrace balance, and unlock your full potential in both your professional and personal life.
Join us as we change the narrative from ‘Burnout’ to ‘Balance’.

speakers.name: Brigette McGregor-Macdonald
speakers.title: Executive Coach and Faciliator
speakers.bio: Brigette is an Executive Coach and Facilitator who helps people cut through life's noise to achieve success. Based in Auckland Brigette has developed an extensive coaching toolkit over the last 20+ years working in the leadership and development field in London, Singapore and now back in New Zealand. Brigette uses curiosity, empathy and toolkit of resources to support people to grow, change and feel less ‘stuck’. Brigette works with people to articulate their vision vs reality and to build a roadmap to tackle challenges. She has a pragmatic business focus and a personal interest and practise in how mindfulness can support business success, resilience and to find more joy in life.

speakers.name: Maja Lee
speakers.title: Customer Performance Marketing Lead, Sky TV
speakers.bio: Maja is a mindful marketing leader, with a track record of driving marketing transformation for global and local brands. After the birth of her daughter, Valentina, Maja founded Foodie Babe, a baby food company focused on vegetables and spices, and she's on a mission to cultivate healthy and adventurous eaters. Currently leading the performance marketing team at Sky TV, Maja loves her work and thrives on connecting fans with top-notch sports and entertainment. She's dedicated to promoting a vibrant and healthy lifestyle, driven by her passion for nutrition, movement, and mindfulness.

coverImage.alt: She Sharp & academyEX International Women's Day 2026 - Together We Can Forge Gender Equality Collectively

events.shortDescription: Join She Sharp and academyEX for an inspiring International Women's Day celebration centred on this year's theme — Give To Gain. An evening of honest conversations, shared experiences, and meaningful connections.

detailPageData.title: She Sharp & academyEX: International Women's Day 2026
detailPageData.subtitle: Celebrating women. Inspiring action. Driving equity.
fullDescription: She Sharp is partnering again with academyEX for International Women's Day 2026, creating space for our community to connect, reflect, and take meaningful action toward gender equality.

This year's IWD theme, Give To Gain, is a reminder that progress grows through community. When we give our time, support, knowledge, and encouragement, we help open doors for women and girls — and everyone benefits.

Join us for a welcoming evening focused on honest conversations, shared experiences, and building connections. This event is about showing up for one another and taking small but meaningful steps together.

speakers.name: Ana Ivanovic-Tongue
speakers.title: Chief Delivery Officer
speakers.bio: Ana Ivanovic-Tongue leads large-scale learning programmes at academyEX, partnering with public and private organisations across New Zealand and Australia. She blends deep programme leadership expertise with a passion for making innovation in learning practical, scalable and human. A member of New Zealand's AI Forum Executive Council, Ana contributes to national conversations on AI adoption and innovation. With 25 years' experience across arts, culture, government, digital transformation and EdTech, plus a Master of Technological Futures focused on AI and art crime, she helps adults build confidence, creativity and resilience in the age of disruption.

speakers.name: Danubi Paim (Dani)
speakers.title: Founder, Property Besties
speakers.bio: Dani Paim bought her first property at 19 with no safety net — just determination and fear. Today she's the founder of Property Besties, New Zealand's most collaborative property investor community (100+ members), and Wealth & Wellness Co., helping women build financial independence without sacrificing what matters most. A former financial advisor, Dani saw women needed clarity, confidence and community — not more information. She left the 9–5 to create supportive, values-driven spaces. She's coached 200+ Kiwis and is on a mission to help 1,000 women invest in property while living fully now, not just at retirement.

speakers.name: Wyndi Tagi
speakers.title: Co-Founder WE Mana & The Table
speakers.bio: Wyndi Tagi is a business strategist, speaker, and community builder passionate about helping people live with purpose and lead with mana. After building and successfully exiting her accounting firm, she now supports purpose-driven founders to grow sustainable businesses without losing themselves in the process. As founder of The Table, a global community for culturally aligned business owners, Wyndi creates spaces where women belong, build, and become. She believes in the power of "Give To Gain" — that when women share wisdom, courage, and support, everyone rises.

speakers.name: Annette Rangi
speakers.title: GM - Digital Transformation
speakers.bio: Annette Rangi is GM of Digital Transformation at HEB Construction, bringing extensive leadership experience across IT, digital delivery, and business transformation. With a career spanning roles as CTO, GM Operations, and Programme Manager across sectors including construction, retail, energy, and government, she champions agile leadership, innovation, and emerging technology adoption. A passionate advocate for diversity, Annette has coached and mentored teams of over 150 people and is experienced in Scaled/Lean-Agile, SAFe, SCRUM, and DevOps methodologies.

speakers.name: Camille Elemia
speakers.title: Journalist turned Product Manager, NZME
speakers.bio: Camille Elemia is an award-winning international journalist turned digital product manager at NZME, where she helps shape the future of digital news experiences at the New Zealand Herald. Over 15 years she reported for The New York Times, BBC, Bloomberg, and Al Jazeera, turning complex global issues into compelling stories. A Fulbright fellow and author of the book Unrequited Love: Duterte's China Embrace, Camille is currently completing a Master of Technological Futures at academyEX, exploring emerging disruptive technologies and their social impact.

detailPageData.title: She Sharp & Candice Murray: Own your Energy!
detailPageData.subtitle: Career Mindset Workshop
fullDescription: How you feel directly impacts how you show up at work and in life.

In this engaging and practical workshop, Career Mindset Coach Candice Murray will guide you through how to consciously choose and access the emotional state that would be most helpful right now — whether that is calm, confidence, self-belief, or happiness.
You will learn powerful, easy-to-use tools that help you shift your energy on demand, so you can perform at your best in the moments that matter, from important conversations to everyday challenges.

The session is designed to be interactive, supportive, and fun, creating a safe space to reflect, participate, and experiment with new ways of thinking and responding. You will leave feeling energised and equipped with practical tools you can immediately apply in both your career and personal life.
Join us for an interactive workshop with Candice Murray - we can’t wait to see you.
✨Know someone who would enjoy this workshop? Feel free to share the event with a friend or colleague and invite them to register.

speakers.name: Candice Murray
speakers.title: Career Mindset Coach
speakers.bio: Candice Murray is a Career Mindset Coach and has been recognised as one of Influence Digest Media's Top Coaches in Auckland for 2025 and 2024. With a down-to-earth approach and real-world expertise, Candice blends practical tools with mindset work to help professionals show up with confidence, clarity and calm — especially in the moments that matter most. She has delivered workshops for organisations including AWS, Spark New Zealand, and AUT University, supporting professionals to build confidence, clarity and momentum. Candice speaks regularly at industry events and facilitates leadership programmes across Aotearoa.

speakers.name: Tim Aynsley
speakers.title: Chief Information Officer
speakers.bio: Tim joined Metlifecare in August 2024 and brings strong digital and technology transformation leadership expertise to the team with over 20 years of experience in senior technology roles, most recently as Head of Technology at Mercury. Tim was a finalist for CIO of the Year in the NZ CIO Awards 2024.

detailPageData.title: HER WAKA — Navigating Pathways into Sustainable Employment
detailPageData.subtitle: AI & The Future of Work — March 2026
fullDescription: Ready to take your next step into meaningful work?

HER WAKA is a dynamic, employment-focused programme delivered by SheSharp in Auckland for Ministry of Social Development clients who are ready to strengthen their pathway into work. Running monthly from March to June 2026, each session is a cohesive, repeatable event designed to build job readiness, confidence, and practical understanding of the New Zealand labour market.

Each two-hour programme brings together up to 25 participants in a supportive, high-impact environment that blends inspiration, practical skills, and direct employer insight. Through real conversations and structured learning, participants gain clarity on how to position themselves confidently and competitively in today's job market.

Our March HER WAKA session focuses on Artificial Intelligence and the evolving tech job market in 2026. Participants can look forward to a dynamic AI Panel Discussion featuring industry professionals, a short hands-on workshop exploring practical AI tools and how they are shaping workplaces, and a special guest speaker from RCSA sharing insights into the 2026 tech hiring landscape and what employers are looking for.
This session will help participants understand how AI is influencing job opportunities, recruitment trends, and the skills that matter most right now.
HER WAKA is more than an event — it is a practical, supportive step toward sustainable employment and long-term workforce participation.
🌟 March 2026 Theme: AI & The Future of Work — our March HER WAKA session focuses on Artificial Intelligence and the evolving tech job market in 2026.
Join us and take your next step forward with confidence. ✨

speakers.name: Nikita Kumari
speakers.title: PMP-certified Product and Project Manager
speakers.bio: Hi, I'm Nikita Kumari — a PMP-certified Product and Project Manager with over 6 years of experience delivering AI and digital products in the B2B SaaS space. I began my career as a Python developer, building a strong technical foundation before moving into product and agile delivery roles. Since then, I've led cross-functional teams and worked with engineers, designers and business stakeholders to turn complex ideas into scalable solutions. My work includes AI and machine learning initiatives for healthcare, research, and enterprise customers.

speakers.name: Chan Meng
speakers.title: Senior AI/ML Infrastructure and Full-Stack Engineer
speakers.bio: Chan Meng is a Senior AI/ML Infrastructure and Full-Stack Engineer specialising in generative AI, autonomous agentic systems, and scalable cloud-native applications. She is a Founding Engineer at Gavigo and CTO at Sanicle. Her work includes advanced RAG architectures, LLM orchestration, and microservices. With a Master's in Applied Computing and a background in mathematics education, Chan combines strong technical expertise with leadership, speaking globally at events including UN CSW69 and mentoring women in STEM.

speakers.name: Meeta Patel
speakers.title: Programme Lead and Lead Facilitator, Leading Change for Good
speakers.bio: Dr Patel is Programme Lead and Lead Facilitator for Leading Change for Good at AcademyEX, with a career spanning industry, research and academia. With a background as a research scientist, she spent many years in applied research before moving into education, reflecting a commitment to learning and community. In this role, she leads and delivers the programme end-to-end, ensuring a meaningful and impactful experience for participants. Outside of professional work, she is an Ambassador for She Sharp, a non-profit organisation focused on bridging the gender gap, and is actively involved in the community, driven by a strong belief in equity and the power of people to create change.

speakers.name: Abe Naus

He is an experienced IT, Projects and Change Recruiter who has been working in recruitment for the past 16 years. His recruitment team's areas of expertise: Project Services, DevOps, Big Data & Analytics, Architects, Developers, Test Analysts, Business Analysts, AI, Agile skilled individuals.

He is passionate about connecting top talent with leading organisations and has a proven ability to build strong relationships with both clients and candidates.

speakers.name: Neekee Reshamwala
speakers.title: Business Manager for Auckland - Randstad Digital
speakers.bio: As the Business Manager for Auckland, Neekee is responsible for driving growth and overseeing daily operations, delivering exceptional results for clients and candidates. Before joining Randstad Digital, Neekee held senior leadership roles in the recruitment industry, where she honed her skills in sales, business development and team management. She holds a Master's degree in Business Management from Massey University and has an in-depth understanding of Auckland's job market.

In this engaging 50-minute workshop, She Sharp Founder and Director Dr Mahsa McCauley (Mohaghegh) will guide participants through practical exercises to help recognise achievements, own your story, and confidently share your impact.

detailPageData.subtitle: Navigating Pathways into Sustainable Employment
fullDescription: The third cohort of the HER WAKA series continues with a session focused on cybersecurity.
🌟 May 2026 Theme: Cybersecurity Workshop — our May HER WAKA session focuses on cybersecurity awareness and the in-demand skills shaping safer digital workplaces.

You will hear from three industry experts through short lightning talks, each sharing their unique perspective and experience in the cybersecurity space. This is an opportunity for participants to gain a broader understanding of the field, the different pathways into it, and the real-world challenges and opportunities it presents.

In the second half of the session, participants will take part in a 45-minute recruiter networking activity with RCSA representatives. There will be 2–3 tables set up where small groups can connect directly with recruiters, ask questions, and practise real-world conversations in a supportive environment.
HER WAKA is more than an event. It is a practical, supportive step toward sustainable employment and long-term workforce participation.
Join us and take your next step forward with confidence. ✨
NOTE: This event is strictly by invitation only.

speakers.name: Paula Gair
speakers.title: Consultant, Educator & Advisor
speakers.bio: Paula specialises in the safe, responsible, and ethical use of technology. She has led digital transformation initiatives for global NGOs and businesses, living and working across 10 countries before returning to Aotearoa, NZ. Her work spans AI, cyber security, privacy, online harm, governance, risk and education. She is focused on strengthening personal and organisational capability through responsible technology use. Her master’s research examined cyber, privacy, and online risk mitigation for non technical audiences. She teaches and supervises at AcademyEX and supports leaders navigating complexity, innovation and disruption (especially in relation to AI).

speakers.name: Swapna Soni
speakers.title: Agile Coach & Change Leader
speakers.bio: Swapna Soni is a Transformation Strategist with 8+ years of experience designing and delivering enterprise-wide change across public and private sectors in New Zealand. She currently serves as Agility Coach at NZ Post, with prior roles at Air New Zealand, Vodafone, and the Ministry of Social Development. Her work spans value-stream-led delivery models, agility-maturity uplift and ADKAR-based change strategies. Swapna brings curiosity, structure and care to help organisations reimagine their operating models and deliver change that sticks.

speakers.name: Prasanth Pavithran
speakers.title: Senior Business Analyst, Office of the CTO
speakers.bio:
Prasanth is a seasoned Information Technology, Strategy, Management, and Business Architecture professional with over 24 years of global experience. Originally from Lutyens’ Delhi in India, he has called New Zealand home for the past 18 years, where he lives with his wife, two children, and their dog. He currently serves as a Senior Business Analyst within the Office of the Chief Technology Officer (OCTO) at Auckland University of Technology (AUT).

Beyond his professional role, Prasanth has spent more than a decade contributing to the New Zealand community through coaching and mentoring professionals. In his personal time, he enjoys the outdoors, playing badminton, and exploring creative writing.

speakers.name: Sian (See-Ann) Clements
speakers.title: Client Relationship & Delivery Partner at Younity
speakers.bio: I’ve spent the past 10+ years in tech recruitment, partnering with businesses to connect them with great people but what really drives me is helping individuals find where they belong in tech. I’m naturally curious. I love understanding how technology works and learning from the people behind it but I’m equally passionate about the human side of it all. With everything changing across AI and emerging tech, I believe there’s never been a more important time to create inclusive pathways into the industry. That’s why being part of “Her Waka” really matters to us at Younity, helping more women step into tech, build confidence, and see where they fit.‍For me, it’s simple: everyone has a place; we just need to help uncover it.

speakers.name: Jenny Martin
speakers.title: Senior Consultant, Potentia
speakers.bio:
With two decades of recruitment experience, I’ve done it all, agency, in-house, hybrid.

I’m a connector at heart; of people, ideas, and opportunities. I use my network intentionally, challenge what doesn’t make sense, and care about doing recruitment well. Being in these shoes, I've learnt empathy, adaptability, and how to truly understand people as individuals.

As a specialist in Permanent IT recruitment at Potentia, I look beyond transactions and instead partner with businesses and talent to make smart, impactful, human decisions.

The right hire doesn’t just fill a role, it changes a business. And the right move doesn’t just increase salary…it changes a life.

specialSections.title: About Her Waka
content: Ready to take your next step into meaningful work?

HER WAKA is a dynamic, employment-focused programme delivered by SheSharp in Auckland for Ministry of Social Development clients who are ready to strengthen their pathway into work. Running monthly from March to June 2026, each session is a cohesive, repeatable event designed to build job readiness, confidence, and practical understanding of the New Zealand labour market.

Each two-hour programme brings together up to 25 participants in a supportive, high-impact environment that blends inspiration, practical skills, and direct employer insight. Through real conversations and structured learning, participants gain clarity on how to position themselves confidently and competitively in today’s job market.

specialSections.title: What to Expect
content: Inspirational speakers sharing authentic employment journeys and practical lessons from navigating the New Zealand workforce
Employer and recruiter panels offering direct insight into current hiring expectations
Practical job-readiness sessions focused on professional presentation, interview confidence, and effective employer engagement
Clear and accessible employment rights guidance
Structured networking opportunities with employers, recruiters, and industry representatives

fullDescription: Discover how AI is helping MYOB teams work smarter, solve problems faster, and deliver more value. This interactive evening brings together students and professionals across development, product, and business teams to explore practical, real-world applications of AI.

Through a speaker session and a hands-on activity, you will see how AI is reshaping the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), explore use cases from across MYOB's business functions, and learn how to develop an AI mindset — understanding both the opportunities and the challenges of adopting AI.

The evening combines insight and practice: hear how MYOB is leveraging AI across the organisation, then put ideas to work in a collaborative AI problem-solving exercise supported by mentors from different MYOB teams.

events.title: Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival 2026 — AUT City Campus

coverImage.alt: Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival 2026 event cover

events.shortDescription: A two-day, in-person hackathon at AUT City Campus where teams build AI-enabled solutions to real-world challenges aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Venue winners advance to national judging and the Aotearoa AI Summit 2026.

detailPageData.title: Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival 2026, hosted by AUT in partnership with She Sharp and the AI Forum
detailPageData.subtitle: Two-Day AI Hackathon

location.address: 55 Wellesley Street East, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010

fullDescription: The Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival is a nationwide, multi-venue hackathon held across Aotearoa New Zealand. She Sharp and the AI Forum are bringing the festival to AUT's City Campus for a two-day, in-person event on 7–8 August 2026.

Working in teams, participants create AI-enabled solutions to real-world challenges aligned to five UN Sustainable Development Goals. Day one focuses on team formation, problem definition, and building; day two on refining solutions and pitching to a local judging panel.

Each venue selects a winning team whose pitch advances to national judging, and four national finalists will be invited to pitch at the Aotearoa AI Summit 2026. No matter your experience level — around a third of participants are new to hackathons — mentors from AUT and industry will support teams throughout.
The festival is about building practical AI capability, encouraging responsible and ethical AI use, fostering collaboration across regions and sectors, and showcasing innovative, impact-driven ideas.

specialSections.title: Two-Day Format
content: Day 1 (Friday 7 August) — Welcome, health & safety briefing, introduction to the hackathon themes, team formation, and the build begins, with ongoing mentor and technical support.
Day 2 (Saturday 8 August) — Continued building, pitch practice, final submissions, live 5-minute pitches to the local judging panel, and announcement of the venue winner.
Venue winners advance to national judging; four national finalists pitch at the Aotearoa AI Summit 2026.

specialSections.title: The Challenge — Five Real-World Themes
content: Tackling food insecurity in a food-exporting nation
Enhancing digital accessibility for all communities
Upskilling the workforce for an AI-driven future
Fostering cross-border, cross-sector collaboration
Honouring indigenous environmental custodianship (kaitiakitanga)

specialSections.title: How the National Festival Works
content: The Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival runs as a series of 48-hour hackathons hosted at venues across Aotearoa New Zealand between 3 and 10 August 2026.
Every venue records its team pitches and selects a local winner. A national judging panel then reviews the winning pitches and selects the finalists.

Four national finalists are invited to pitch live at the Aotearoa AI Summit on 18 September 2026 in Auckland, where the Summit audience votes for the winning solution and the award-winning team is announced.

specialSections.title: 2026 Venues
content: Auckland — AUT City Campus, hosted by AUT + She Sharp, 7–8 August (this event)
Auckland — AUT, hosted by AUT + Tū Ātea, 7–8 August
Auckland — Mission Ready, 5–6 August
Auckland — Unitec, with Seen Ventures, 6–8 August
Waikato — Te Ipu o Te Mahara | Artificial Intelligence Institute, 6–7 August
Wellington — Amazon Web Services (AWS), 6–7 August
Christchurch — EPIC Innovation + Canterbury Tech, 6–7 August
More venues to be announced.

specialSections.title: Why Attend
content: Build practical, hands-on AI capability on real-world problems
Collaborate in diverse teams (3–7 people) with mentor and technical support
Learn responsible and ethical AI practices
Pitch your solution and compete to represent your venue at national judging
Open to all experience levels — beginners are welcome

specialSections.title: Live Q&A Sessions
content: Session 1 — Wednesday 1 July 2026, 12:00–1:00pm NZST, online live stream, hosted by Christina Tombs. Mentors and venue hosts answer your questions about the rules of engagement, ideas, technology and how to take part.
Save the date and join via the AUT City Campus Community Hub — more lunchtime sessions follow through July.

specialSections.title: Registration
content: Register online at aihackathon.nz.
Concession and complimentary places are available for AUT students, mentors and supporting staff — registration details are shared directly via the AUT City Campus Community Hub.
Enter as a team or as an individual — just let us know which when you register, and we will help solo registrants find a team on the day.
Join the AUT City Campus Community Hub for the latest updates and live Q&A session dates.

infoSections.title: About the Festival — AI for Good
paragraphs: Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival is a nationwide kaupapa built around one idea: AI for good — building solutions that matter. Over an intense weekend, diverse teams turn real-world challenges into working, AI-enabled prototypes.
Hackathons are a safe space for a wide range of people to unite and solve problems. Building a team with a variety of skills — not just coding — is the surest path to a strong pitch.

images.alt: An unfurling silver fern koru, symbolising new growth

infoSections.title: Part of a Nationwide Festival
paragraphs: The AUT City Campus event is one of several venues running across the country during the festival window in early August 2026.
Venues span Auckland, Waikato, Wellington and Christchurch — see the 2026 Venues list above for the host and dates at each location, with more to be announced.

infoSections.title: Live Q&A & Community Hub
paragraphs: The festival hosts online lunchtime Q&A sessions covering the rules of engagement, ideas, problems to solve, datasets and technology — everything you need to prepare. The first session is on Wednesday 1 July 2026, 12:00–1:00pm NZST, hosted by Christina Tombs.
Join the AUT City Campus Community Hub for the live stream link and future session dates, or subscribe to the AI Forum mailing list for updates.

infoSections.title: About the Venue
paragraphs: The event is hosted in person at AUT City Campus, 55 Wellesley Street East, in the heart of Auckland's CBD — well served by public transport and within walking distance of the city centre.
Please bring your own laptop and charger. Power, Wi-Fi, mentoring and refreshments are provided on site across both days.
